instruction: Set up visual notifications by making the screen blink during audio alerts.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: VISUAL_BELL=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences visual-bell 2>/dev/null | grep -c true); if [ "$VISUAL_BELL" -gt 0 ]; then echo "Visual alerts enabled"; else echo "Visual alerts disabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: This task requires enabling visual alerts (visual bell). The evaluator checks if org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences visual-bell is set to true. When enabled, the screen flashes instead of playing an audible alert beep, which is helpful for users who are deaf or hard of hearing. This is similar in difficulty to the original task - both require navigating accessibility settings and enabling a single feature. No custom functions needed as we use existing check_include_exclude metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts the visual-bell setting state using gsettings command
Metric comparison logic (check_include_exclude) appropriately verifies the presence of success message and absence of failure messages
Complete coverage: single requirement (enable visual alerts) is fully verified by checking the visual-bell setting
Robust error handling with timeout and error detection in exclude list
Expected values are semantically correct: includes 'Visual alerts enabled', excludes 'Visual alerts disabled' and 'error'
Data flow is correct: command output → metric checks for correct patterns → returns appropriate score
No parameter handling issues: metric receives rules dictionary directly when expected.type='rule'
